Kintec Motors Announces $220 Million Expansion of Thai Manufacturing Facility

Kintec Motors has unveiled plans to invest $220 million in expanding its automotive assembly operations in Rayong, Thailand, underscoring the country’s growing significance as a regional manufacturing hub. The project will increase the plant’s annual production capacity by 35%, with completion targeted for late 2025, according to a company statement released Thursday.

The expansion will add two new assembly lines and a state-of-the-art paint shop, supporting both internal combustion and electric vehicle platforms. Kintec Motors expects to create over 800 new jobs as a result of the initiative, including skilled technical and engineering positions.

“Thailand remains central to our growth strategy in Southeast Asia,” said Marta Li, Kintec’s VP of Manufacturing for Asia-Pacific. “This investment not only enables us to meet rising demand across the region, but also affirms our commitment to supporting the Thai government’s vision for advanced automotive production and sustainable mobility.”

Thailand is the largest vehicle producer in Southeast Asia and has been actively promoting investment in next-generation automotive technologies. The country’s Board of Investment (BOI) has rolled out a suite of incentives for automakers, including tax breaks and grants for projects that incorporate electric vehicle components and environmentally friendly processes.

“The continued expansion of global players like Kintec Motors speaks to the competitiveness of Thailand’s supply chain and workforce,” said Jirawat Thongchai, director of the Thai Automotive Institute. “With the industry shifting towards electric vehicles and smart manufacturing, these investments are vital for maintaining our position as a leading exporter.”

The Kintec facility currently manufactures sport utility vehicles and compact sedans, with approximately 60% of output destined for export markets such as Australia, Indonesia, and the Philippines. The company plans to introduce two new hybrid models following the expansion, aligning with Thailand’s national goal of producing 30% zero-emission vehicles by 2030.

Local suppliers are also expected to benefit from increased volumes and new sourcing opportunities. “Our members welcome the expansion as it promises higher orders and the chance to participate in more sophisticated value chains,” said Supachai Rattanasuk, president of the Eastern Automotive Parts Association.

Construction is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2024. The BOI has confirmed that Kintec’s project qualifies for its current EV and green technology incentive scheme. Industry observers note that further investments by international OEMs are likely as Thailand continues to position itself at the forefront of automotive innovation in the region.
